slides.headline: What does secured mean?
slides.body: Secured business loans use property, equipment or other business assets as collateral, which reduces risk for the lender. In exchange, this structure can support larger loan amounts, longer repayment terms and potentially sharper pricing than an unsecured facility of the same size, depending on the asset and lender.

caption:
Offering security doesn't just reduce lender risk — depending on the asset and lender, it can also open the door to larger facilities, longer terms, and potentially sharper pricing than an equivalent unsecured loan.

Property, equipment and other business assets can all be considered, with loan-to-value ratios and documentation requirements varying by lender and asset type.

Curious what your assets could support? Let's talk it through.

General information only. This does not constitute financial, legal, accounting or tax advice. Credit is subject to lender assessment, eligibility and approval criteria. Fees, charges, terms and conditions may apply.
